content.markdown:
# Testing sparse-data product recommendations against best-seller sorting

## Verified facts
- Harmat reports datasets ranging from around 520 to 1,900 completed orders, cannot wait for larger datasets, and found best-seller sorting superior to collaborative filtering in one client’s A/B test. [F1]
- Harmat wants an initial prototype for one client. Its offered access covers anonymised transactions and product catalogues under a data-sharing agreement; additional behavioural tracking is not part of that stated offer. [F2]
- Harmat can allocate roughly one mid-level developer-day weekly. Its environment includes WooCommerce/custom REST integrations and Docker deployments on client VPS environments; additional serving infrastructure is not established. [F3]
- Erić lists openness to joint projects with retail technology companies, but cautions against commitments exceeding one day weekly outside the faculty during semester. [F4]
- Erić’s research offers a concrete candidate: combining cosine similarity of product attributes with basket co-occurrence. That study used 9,200 baskets from two clothing retailers, not Harmat’s smaller client datasets. [F5]
- Her review identifies over-specialisation as a content-based recommendation risk. Her benchmarking work specifies temporal splitting, single-purchase-user treatment and discontinued-product handling. [F6]

## Potential benefits
- For the company: Harmat could learn whether existing catalogue information supports a worthwhile alternative to best-sellers, or whether further recommendation development is unjustified at present.
- For the researcher: Subject to agreement, Erić could test the boundary of attribute–behaviour hybrids at smaller transaction volumes using an approved client dataset and practical integration feedback.

## Our inference
- This suggests a lightweight joint project could test whether metadata compensates for sparse purchases without assuming that a hybrid must win. Transfer to this client’s catalogue, languages and smaller order volume remains unvalidated.
- The proposal is conditional because Erić’s actual availability is unconfirmed. Limited engineering time suggests starting with precomputed recommendations rather than assuming new serving infrastructure.
- Offline purchase ranking could establish technical promise, but likely cannot establish widget conversion or revenue gains. Sparse evaluation data may leave the result inconclusive.

## Proposed next steps
- Propose a six-week first experiment on one approved client’s existing orders and catalogue. Harmat would prepare anonymised exports and review catalogue languages; Erić would design evaluation and models. Audit attributes, timestamps and availability; create chronological training, tuning and untouched evaluation samples, checking independence and leakage. Use an explicit matrix: popularity baseline; attributes only; co-occurrence only; attributes plus co-occurrence. Tune only before evaluation, without importing published weights. Measure precision at three on confirmed held-out co-purchases, coverage, uncertainty and expert-rated substitute/complement usefulness; missing purchases are not definitive negatives. Propose a 10% relative precision improvement over popularity, with a positive confidence-bound difference, as a negotiable target. Go only if the best tested configuration meets agreed usefulness and coverage criteria using existing data, agreed budget, developer allocation and hosting limits; otherwise stop or report inconclusive. Offline success would authorise prototype testing, not a claim of business uplift.
- Subject to the gate, propose precomputed recommendations exposed through the existing integration. Benchmark resource use, latency and refresh effort on the agreed VPS, review user-facing languages, and document maintenance. Any additional infrastructure would require approval rather than being assumed.
- Agree a traffic-feasible online comparison against best-sellers only after reviewing prior A/B results. Predefine the company’s business metric, minimum worthwhile improvement and uncertainty rule; do not expand deployment without meeting that criterion. If traffic is insufficient, report the business effect as unresolved.

## Open questions
- Can Erić confirm availability, start timing and semester-compatible allocation, including whether periodic anonymised refreshes would meet her collaboration interests?
- Which client can approve participation, and what usable baskets, catalogue attributes, languages, timestamps and identifiers can be shared under agreed access, retention and derived-model safeguards?
- Should recommendations prioritise substitutes, complements or both, and what business metric, minimum improvement, coverage and uncertainty criteria should govern progression?
- What budget, deadline, VPS and latency limits, refresh expectations and maintenance ownership are acceptable, and can Harmat share prior A/B results and traffic volumes?
